ABOUT

THE WHAT AND HOW

I'm a community ecologist studying how ecological communities assemble: who interacts with whom, why, and what happens when those relationships are disrupted. My research focuses primarily on plants and pollinators while extending to herbivores, seed dispersers, and the broader web of interactions that sustains ecological communities. I combine experiments, observational studies, large datasets, and models to address these questions.

Much of my work explores how ecological communities change through time and how historical contingencies shape their trajectories. If ecological processes are inherently context-dependent, how can our models account for the particular conditions and histories from which they emerge?

Increasingly, I find myself questioning not only what science we do, but how we do it. I aim to embrace slower, more thoughtful processes and help create greater visibility and more equitable opportunities for women and Global South communities in science.

RESEARCH

PROJECTS

Present and future research projects

+ Add photo


COMMUNITY DISASSEMBLY

GANANCIA Y PÉRDIDA DE ESPECIES

¿Qué sucede cuando una especie entra en una comunidad o desaparece de ella? Estudio cómo responden las comunidades a la pérdida de especies—incluidas las remociones selectivas durante procesos de restauración—y a la incorporación de nuevas especies mediante invasiones de plantas, preguntándome cómo afecta cada proceso a la vegetación y a las redes planta–polinizador.

+ Add photo


CLIMATE CHANGE

COMMUNITIES IN A WARMING WORLD

Climate warming is altering which species coexist and how plant communities are structured. Using long-term datasets, functional traits, and ecological models, I examine these shifts across environmental gradients and investigate the processes driving them (or not).

+ Add photo


PHENOLOGICAL REASSEMBLY

TIMING, ORDER, AND PRIORITY EFFECTS

Climate-driven shifts in flowering can change the order in which species appear and interact. I investigate how this altered timing creates priority effects, influences plant–pollinator interactions, and sets communities on different ecological trajectories.

+ Add photo


HERBARIA

CHANGING CALENDARS

Herbarium specimens offer a window into the past, revealing how plants responded to changing environments. I am developing a comparative project combining flowering records, plant traits, and evidence of pollination to understand climate-driven change across mountain regions. With collaborators in Argentina, Switzerland, and the United States, I hope to expand this work to other regions and ecological interactions.

+ Add photo

Illustration: “Feeling Extra Latina Hoy” by Ana Raquel

INCLUSIVE SCIENCE

OPENING PATHWAYS IN ECOLOGY

I am developing an initiative that connects women and researchers from the Global South through mentoring, peer exchange, and accessible research resources. It aims to reduce barriers to training, funding, international networks, and visibility while creating space for more diverse voices to shape ecological research.

Explore the resources so far and get in touch if you’d like to join. LowCostEcology (pilot) ↗
